KEY MESSAGE 1...Brief period of showers mainly Fri morning with a 
lull in the activity much of Fri afternoon outside of a few spot 
showers. Cluster of showers & perhaps a few embedded t-storms with 
even a low risk for severe weather between 5 and 11 pm Fri evening.
Windy and much cooler Sat with highs in the lower-middle 50s.

Large high pressure shifts east of the region tonight as an 
intensifying low pressure moves across the eastern Great Lakes. This 
will allow a return southerly flow of air along with increasing low 
level moisture to work northward into the region overnight. 
Initially...mainly clear skies/light winds will allow for temps to 
fall quickly through the 40s in many locations shortly after sunset 
this evening. However...increasing clouds along with developing low 
level southeast flow will allow for slowly rising temperatures 
toward daybreak.

In addition...the developing southerly LLJ/moisture transport will 
increase the forcing for ascent and allow for a cluster of showers 
to develop toward daybreak across interior southern New England. 
These showers may reach the coastal plain during the early-mid 
morning hours. The showers should be fairly numerous especially 
across northern MA...but the steady showers should be relatively 
short-lived lasting generally 1-3 hours in a given location. 
Otherwise...a good portion of Fri afternoon should feature a lull in 
the activity. A few spot showers certainly will remain 
possible...But much of this period may feature just cloudy skies 
with a breezy southerly wind. Despite lots of clouds...strong warm 
advection should push highs well into the 60s in many locations 
perhaps even near 70 in few spots. Dewpoints reaching or breaking 
60+ will result in a bit of humidity too for the middle of October 
standards. 

The main concern though is between 5 and 11 pm Fri evening as a cold 
front crosses the region. There should be roughly a few hundred J/KG 
of at least elevated Cape ahead of this front. Strong jet 
dynamics/forcing are also depicted ahead of this front with 55-65 
knots of effective shear. The high resolution models generally show 
a line of showers with perhaps some embedded thunder as the cold 
front sweeps across the region. Despite very strong jet 
dynamics...instability is meager...so the severe weather potential 
is low but brief sub-severe wind gusts of 35-50 mph are still 
possible even if the showers do not contain any thunder. 
However...if we end up getting just a bit better moisture return off 
the relatively warm ocean...the low risk for severe weather could be 
realized. The CSU machine learning probabilities as well as the NCAR 
HRRR neural network indicate a low risk for severe weather. Again 
this is a low probability...but it needs to be watched. The main 
risk would be locally strong to damaging wind gusts especially with 
fully leafed trees across most locations.

Otherwise...a much cooler airmass works into the region late Fri 
night and Saturday on quite gusty NW winds. A few lingering showers 
possible into mid-morning Sat near the southeast New England coast. 
Otherwise...windy with northwest wind gusts on the order of 25 to 35 
mph with a few gusts near 40 mph expected on Sat. Despite skies 
becoming partly sunny on Sat...highs will be held in the lower to 
middle 50s. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Chilly night Saturday night with below-freezing
low temperatures away from the coasts.

After a cool, dry and blustery Saturday, looking at one of the 
coldest nights we've seen to this point in autumn 2026 as broad, and 
strong high pressure settles in over the Northeast. It's still a 
little unclear how quickly the blustery NW winds from the daytime 
hours subside but at least very good radiational cooling conditions 
are anticipated. With a likely cool start, should see lows drop into 
mid 20s to low 30s range for much of Southern New England except in 
the mid 30s for the cities and Cape Cod/Islands. Note that the 
frost/freeze program for Southern New England has ended as of 
October 11th and not expected to resume again until mid-Spring 2027, 
which means freeze/frost headlines won't be issued; however if you 
still have plants/crops outside, you'll want to take the necessary 
precautions to prevent freeze/frost damage. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Dry with a modest warmup through early next 
week, though monitoring coastal storminess near or south of the 
mid- Atlantic waters. 

The expansive surface high pressure from Saturday night, spanning 
from the Southern Appalachians through Southern New England and the 
Canadian Maritimes, then governs our weather pattern Sunday through 
early next week. This will facilitate a steady warming trend with 
slightly above normal temperatures, with mostly clear skies and 
strong diurnal temperature ranges (milder days, cool nights). 
Looking at highs Sunday in the mid to upper 50s and lows in the 30s.
